calibrationDelta.priorGate: The twelve V7 Mercury masters passed the prior gate before the owner rejected them on a cold rendered read.
calibrationDelta.newGate: 8/12 V7 pages rejected; 0/1 Sun-in-Leo V3 gold passed.
calibrationDelta.contextIsolation: The cold pass received rendered_copy only; no meaning plan, source note, astrology logic, intended meaning, or drafting context was sent.

results.reason: The copy reads clearly and naturally from start to finish. Each section follows logically, uses concrete examples, and keeps the advice direct without relying on awkward or overly abstract phrasing.
Several lines rely on unexplained astrological shorthand or vague references, and one sentence uses an abstract metaphor that makes the practical point harder to understand.

violations.text: Taurus changes Mercury’s standard.
violations.reason: Cold, this does not state a clear idea in ordinary language. A reader who does not already know how these terms relate has to infer what is changing and what “Mercury’s standard” means.
violations.revision_instruction: State the practical shift directly, without relying on the relationship between the two astrological terms to carry the meaning.

violations.text: This works well when a decision needs more than enthusiasm behind it.
violations.reason: “This” has no precise referent. It could mean the transit, the preceding questions, or a general approach, so the reader has to stop and resolve it.
violations.revision_instruction: Replace the vague referent with the specific approach or behavior being described.

violations.text: Mercury in Taurus is good at noticing the difference between an idea that sounds reassuring and one that can actually support the life built around it.
violations.reason: The phrase “support the life built around it” is abstract and strained. It is unclear how an idea supports a life, requiring the reader to translate the intended practical meaning.
violations.revision_instruction: Name the concrete practical test or consequence directly instead of using the “life built around it” metaphor.

results.reason: Several lines use abstract or unnatural phrasing that makes the reader translate the meaning rather than receive it directly.

violations.text: Let the information move
violations.reason: This is too abstract to communicate a clear action or idea on first read. A reader has to infer what “information move” means in practice.
violations.revision_instruction: Replace the abstract phrase with a plain-language heading that names the behavior or benefit directly.

violations.text: Gemini changes Mercury’s range.
violations.reason: “Changes Mercury’s range” is vague and sounds like astrology shorthand rather than normal reader-facing prose. The reader is not told what kind of range is changing.
violations.revision_instruction: State the specific change in plain language rather than referring broadly to Mercury’s “range.”

violations.text: Change your mind when the facts improve
violations.reason: Facts do not ordinarily “improve.” The intended idea is understandable, but the wording is unnatural and makes the reader pause.
violations.revision_instruction: Use everyday wording that refers to receiving better information, stronger evidence, or new facts.

violations.text: Mercury in Gemini makes room for the possibility that better information should change what gets said next.
violations.reason: “Makes room for the possibility” is indirect and abstract, and “what gets said next” is awkwardly vague. The sentence takes a simple point and states it in a formal, roundabout way.
violations.revision_instruction: State directly that new or better information can change the conclusion or response.

violations.text: The connection gets found, but nobody else understands it because the explanation skipped the middle.
violations.reason: “The connection gets found” is unnatural passive phrasing, and “skipped the middle” is compressed shorthand. The reader can infer the point, but a normal writer would name the missing steps in the explanation.
violations.revision_instruction: Use active, everyday language that says someone found a link but did not explain the steps connecting it to the conclusion.

results.reason: A few lines rely on vague or compressed phrasing that makes the reader pause to infer the intended meaning.

violations.location: Paragraph beginning “Memory can catch what the literal wording misses”
violations.text: This works well when the important part of a conversation is not stated directly.
violations.reason: “This” has no clear, immediate referent. The reader has to infer whether it means Mercury in Cancer, memory, or the ability to notice subtext.
violations.revision_instruction: Replace “This” with a direct noun phrase that names the specific ability or situation being described.

violations.location: Paragraph beginning “The past can answer before the present does”
violations.text: The complication is letting recognition become proof.
violations.reason: “Recognition become proof” is compressed and abstract. A reader has to translate it into the more concrete idea of treating a familiar pattern or feeling as evidence that the same problem is happening again.
violations.revision_instruction: State directly that the problem is assuming a current pause or message means the same thing as a past one before checking the facts.

violations.text: Scorpio changes Mercury’s method. Mercury becomes less interested in taking the first explanation at face value.

violations.text: Attention goes toward what is missing, what changed, what was left unanswered, and what shows up when separate pieces of information are compared.
violations.reason: “Attention goes toward” sounds formal and assembled rather than like ordinary prose. The long list also makes the sentence feel indirect.
violations.revision_instruction: Use a more natural verb and state plainly what the reader is likely to notice or examine.

results.reason: Several lines rely on abstract or unclear phrasing that a reader cannot understand directly without supplying the missing connection.

violations.location: Paragraph under “Name the larger point,” first sentence
violations.text: Sagittarius changes Mercury’s scale.

violations.location: Paragraph under “Give the information a direction,” final sentence
violations.text: The facts gain direction because people understand why they matter.
violations.reason: “Facts gain direction” is abstract and unnatural. Facts do not literally gain direction, so the reader must translate the phrase to understand the point.
violations.revision_instruction: Name the practical result in plain language, such as how understanding why the facts matter helps people use them or decide what to do.

violations.text: Check how much the facts really support
violations.reason: The heading leaves out what the facts are supposed to support. It reads as incomplete and forces the reader to supply the missing object.
violations.revision_instruction: Specify plainly what the facts should support, so the heading stands on its own.

violations.text: While Mercury is in Sagittarius, make the connection and say the bigger point out loud.

violations.revision_instruction: Identify the connection directly, such as connecting the details to the larger point or conclusion.

results.reason: Several lines use unclear or strained phrasing that makes the reader infer the concrete meaning, especially around approval, identity, and the Leo-to-Virgo transition.

violations.text: Soon the work is no longer becoming more honest or more interesting. It is becoming easier to approve.
violations.reason: The work is described as "becoming" honest, interesting, and easier to approve, which is indirect and mechanically phrased. It is also unclear who is doing the approving.
violations.revision_instruction: Name the change in the creator's choices directly and clarify whose approval is being sought.

violations.text: The version that gets rewarded can still be the wrong version to keep feeding.
violations.reason: "Keep feeding" is an unclear metaphor for maintaining or reinforcing an identity. A reader has to translate it to understand the point.
violations.revision_instruction: Replace the feeding metaphor with a direct, everyday description of continuing to perform or support an inauthentic version of oneself.

violations.text: What we name during Leo season is what Virgo season will ask us to build.
violations.reason: It is unclear what "we name" refers to, and the phrase "Virgo season will ask us to build" is abstract and personifies the season rather than stating the practical connection.
violations.revision_instruction: Specify what is being named and state plainly how that choice connects to the work that follows.

violations.text: The work worth carrying forward is the work we still mean when the spotlight is off.
violations.reason: "The work we still mean" is not a natural everyday phrase. The reader must infer that it means work they still believe in or stand behind without attention.
violations.revision_instruction: Use a more ordinary, direct phrase for continuing to believe in or stand behind the work without public attention.
